main_body: A small chest or crate. It has an orange banded lid (rows 1-7), a dark band at row 8, a brown and gold front (rows 9-10), and a dark base with yellow-black checks (rows 11-13).
top_band: Rows 1-3 run orange, #b85a1c to #f09a40 (L 111-169), and are darker than the lid face below. Row 4 is a dark #b85a1c line. Rows 5-7 are light #ffc26a/#f09a40 (L 169-202). The top is not the lightest tone and does not read as a horizontal surface.
evidence: The scan is identical at x=4, 8 and 11. It shows stacked horizontal bands with alternating tones (111, 141, 169, 111, 202, 169, 202), which read as slats or planks seen face-on. The darkest-to-lightest gradient in rows 1-3 looks like a curved lid front, not a top surface seen from above. The lighter band at rows 5-7 is a vertical face. No distinct lighter top plane is separated from the front by a clear edge line. The dark row 8 is a band on the face, not an eave shadow over a visible top. The checker pattern at rows 11-13 is painted flat. The drawing is a front elevation of a chest, so the top is not clearly seen from above.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 12 colours per tile against 17-20. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral (#06070e and #20202a), so the outline is a near-black sticker line, unlike the tinted outlines of the references. The orange ramp has about 5 steps and flat-fill coverage is 0%, but the palette is thin and the material variety is low (a single orange ramp plus dark, gold and blue-grey accents). It would look thinner and more sticker-like beside the references.
